function_v0.doc:
Settle trader PnL with the vault.
Called by the Market contract when positions are closed.

# Arguments
* `pnl` - Profit/loss amount (positive = trader won, negative = trader lost)

# Settlement Logic

**Trader WON (pnl > 0):**
- Vault transfers profit amount to Market contract
- Market then pays trader: collateral + profit
- Vault's total_usdc decreases by pnl

**Trader LOST (pnl < 0):**
- Only update accounting here (Vault cannot pull from Market)
- Market must call `receive_loss()` separately to transfer the loss
- This respects Soroban's auth model: contracts can only spend own tokens

**Break-even (pnl = 0):**
- No transfers needed, just emit event
Returns the profit actually paid out. A winner's close can never
hard-revert here: the payout is capped at what the pool holds and
any unpaid remainder is booked as a CLAIMABLE per-trader shortfall
(L0-3: repaid from future buffer inflows via claim_shortfall).
Losses are credited ONLY when the USDC actually arrives, via
receive_loss.

\xe2\x9a\xa0\xef\xb8\x8f ABI: (env, trader,
function_v0.name: settle_pnl

function_v0.doc:
Cover bankrupt-liquidation losses from the insurance buffer (L0-2).
Market-only. ACCOUNTING-ONLY \xe2\x80\x94 no token moves: the bad-debt USDC was
never collected, and the buffer's tokens already sit in the vault.
Moving `covered` from the buffer bucket into total_usdc offsets the
NAV drop the uncollected loss causes at close, 1:1 \xe2\x80\x94 NOE price stays
flat when the buffer covers and falls by exactly the LP-absorbed
remainder when it cannot. Returns the covered amount.

Spend rule: the ShortfallReserve is a DISJOINT bucket (never inside
BufferBalance), so every buffer spender \xe2\x80\x94 winner payouts in
settle_pnl, this draw, claim_shortfall's buffer leg \xe2\x80\x94 reads the same
BufferBalance and can never touch earmarked repayment funds.
function_v0.name: draw_buffer

function_v0.doc:
Receive loss payment from Market contract.
Called by Market after settle_pnl() when trader loses.

# Arguments

# Flow
1. Market calls settle_pnl(negative_pnl) - updates accounting
2. Market transfers loss amount to Vault
3. Market calls receive_loss(amount) - Vault verifies receipt

This function is optional but recommended for verification.
The accounting was already updated in settle_pnl().

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Per-market risk parameters (L0-12). Stored per asset in market storage
(DataKey::AssetRisk) and read on the hot path \xe2\x80\x94 no cross-contract call.
Invariant mm_bps == im_bps/2 (P5-2), enforced by is_valid() at the
admin setter. The `close_out_bps` and funding/skew fields are consumed
by L0-5 / L0-13 / L0-14 respectively but MUST be in the day-one layout:
Soroban decodes structs by exact field set, so adding a field later
re-bricks every stored entry.
udt_struct_v0.name: AssetRiskParams

fields.doc: Full-close band, bps of notional (< mm_bps) \xe2\x80\x94 consumed by L0-5.
fields.name: close_out_bps

fields.doc: Funding rate ceiling, bps/HOUR \xe2\x80\x94 consumed by L0-13.
fields.name: funding_clamp_bps

fields.doc: Initial margin, bps of notional (400 = 4% = 25x implied).
fields.name: im_bps

fields.doc: Funding velocity ceiling, bps/DAY \xe2\x80\x94 consumed by L0-13.
fields.name: max_funding_velocity_bps

fields.doc: Explicit leverage cap; may sit BELOW 10000/im_bps (launch policy).
fields.name: max_leverage

fields.doc: Max position size, 7-decimal USD notional.
fields.name: max_position_size

fields.doc: Maintenance margin, bps; invariant mm == im/2.
fields.name: mm_bps

fields.doc: SIP-279 skew scale, 7-decimal USD notional (\xe2\x89\x88 2\xc3\x97 the OI cap) \xe2\x80\x94 L0-13.
fields.name: skew_scale

fields.doc: Total initial margin used by cross positions (7 decimals)
fields.name: used_margin

udt_struct_v0.doc: The `level` view (architecture \xc2\xa711): the counters and the queue depth\n(`slots.len()`, the next seq to be assigned).
udt_struct_v0.name: LevelInfo

udt_struct_v0.doc:
`quote_place` output: the simulate step of the client protocol (\xc2\xa714). `keys`
is every PageBook key the walk and a possible rest can touch on both sides
(band levels visited, words start..limit, summaries, bests, own-side rest
keys, fee accruals); the client adds `Order(taker, nonce)`, both vault
balances, the pad band, and marks archived keys for restore from RPC
(ADR-020).
udt_struct_v0.name: QuoteResult

udt_struct_v0.doc: One level the simulated walk visited, with its open lots at simulation.
udt_struct_v0.name: CrossedLevel

udt_error_enum_v0.doc: Codes are stable: 12 (`RetryRest`), 19 (`BadWindow`) and 22\n(`CorruptEntry`) were retired with slot windows and pages (ADR-037) and are\nnot reused.
udt_error_enum_v0.name: Error

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One price level's FIFO queue (architecture \xc2\xa72): counters plus the quantity
slots of the current generation, all in one entry (ADR-037). `slots.len()`
is the tail: appends push, a sweep or empty-level reset empties the vector,
so the entry is exactly as large as the queue is deep (124 B empty, 12 B
per slot). Slot `s` lives at index `s`. A slot at or past the head holds
the order's *open* lots: a partial take decrements the head slot in place,
and a zero slot, whether a cancel or consumption put it there, is skipped.
Slots behind the head are never read and may hold stale values; only
`slots[head_seq..]` is meaningful.
udt_struct_v0.name: Level

udt_struct_v0.doc: Venue configuration (architecture \xc2\xa71). Instance storage; a plain named\nstruct \xe2\x80\x94 its rent rides on the instance TTL the `keepalive` crank pays, so\nthe map encoding's extra bytes cost nothing that matters (ADR-022).
udt_struct_v0.name: Config

udt_struct_v0.doc: Per-market parameters (architecture \xc2\xa71). Written at creation and by\n`set_market_caps` only, read (free) by every op: a named struct, not a\npacked body \xe2\x80\x94 one-time rent per market is the only cost (ADR-022).
udt_struct_v0.name: Market

udt_struct_v0.doc: Best tick per side (architecture \xc2\xa75): `empty` set means no recorded best.\nWritten on most takes and many rests, but at ~56 B the map encoding costs\ntens of stroops per write; readability wins (ADR-022).
udt_struct_v0.name: BestTick
